KinesioCal Provider Terms of Service

Last updated 11/09/2026

1. Agreement and Definitions

These Terms of Service ("Terms") are a binding agreement between KinesioCal, LLC, an Indiana limited liability company ("KinesioCal," "we," "us"), and the business or individual that creates an account ("Subscriber," "you"). By creating an account or using the Service, you accept these Terms. If you accept on behalf of a business, you represent that you have authority to bind it.

  • Service — the KinesioCal software platform, including scheduling, booking portals, client records, notes, and related features, websites, APIs, and support.
  • Subscriber — the business entity or sole proprietor holding the account (the tenant). Subscriber is responsible for all Users on its account.
  • User — any individual the Subscriber authorizes to access the Service (owners, practitioners, staff).
  • Client — a member of the public who books, receives, or pays for Subscriber's services through the Service. Clients are not parties to these Terms; their use of public booking portals is governed by the Client Terms and the Privacy Policy.
  • Subscriber Data — all data Subscriber or its Users or Clients enter into or generate through the Service, including Client records.
  • Licensed Services — massage therapy, bodywork, and other services that require a professional license, certification, or registration in the jurisdiction where they are performed.

2. Eligibility, Accounts, and Licensure

You must be at least 18 years old and operate a lawful business to subscribe. You are responsible for keeping credentials confidential and for all activity under your account. Notify us promptly at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com of any unauthorized access; if your report would include Client health information, send it through the Contact support form in the app instead of email.

Licensure representations. By using the Service to offer Licensed Services, you represent and warrant, on a continuing basis, that:

  1. Every individual who performs Licensed Services through your account holds a current, valid license, certification, or registration in good standing in each jurisdiction where the services are performed.
  2. Your business holds all establishment, local, and municipal permits required to operate at each service location, including mobile or outcall services.
  3. You will update practitioner licensure information in the Service yourself within 30 days of any change, lapse, suspension, or discipline. The Service does not track license expirations or remind you.
  4. We may check practitioner credentials against public licensing-board records during a review under Section 4, and may suspend any practitioner profile or account that cannot be verified.

We do not verify licensure as a service to Clients, and inclusion in the Service is not an endorsement by KinesioCal.

3. Prohibited Businesses and Uses

KinesioCal exists to serve legitimate, licensed service professionals. The following are strictly prohibited and will result in immediate termination without refund.

3.1 Illicit touch services. You may not use the Service to advertise, schedule, book, record, bill, pay staff for, or otherwise facilitate, directly or indirectly:

  • sexual services of any kind, whether or not legal in the jurisdiction, including any service in which sexual contact, sexual stimulation, or nudity for sexual purposes is offered, implied, or expected as part of the service or as a tip, upgrade, or add-on;
  • human trafficking, forced labor, debt bondage, or the recruitment, transport, harboring, or control of any person for such purposes;
  • services by any person under 18, or any sexual content or contact involving a minor;
  • any service by a person who does not hold the license required for that service, or any "massage" or "bodywork" business operating without a required establishment permit.

3.2 Indicators we treat as evidence of violation. We may treat the following as grounds for investigation or action under Section 4, alone or in combination:

  • services, menu items, or pricing that reference sexual acts by name, euphemism, or coded terminology;
  • practitioner profiles listing no verifiable license, or licenses that cannot be matched to the named individual;
  • booking patterns inconsistent with licensed practice (for example, 24-hour operation, "any available" practitioner selection with no license shown, or client notes requesting prohibited services);
  • staff who cannot be matched to the business's staff records; who reside at a commercial service location or in housing arranged or controlled by the business; whose identification documents are held by the business; or who cannot, when asked during a Section 4 review, document that they are legally authorized to work in the jurisdiction where services are performed. A licensed practitioner operating from their own residence, or a sole proprietor whose business address is their home, is not an indicator under this item;
  • credible reports from Clients, staff, licensing boards, or law enforcement;
  • any attempt to obscure the above, including deleting records after a report.

3.3 Other prohibited uses. You may not: (a) use the Service in violation of any law, including professional-licensing, labor, tax, and consumer-protection law; (b) upload malicious code or attempt to breach or probe the Service's security; (c) scrape, resell, sublicense, or white-label the Service; (d) reverse engineer or copy the Service's features, data models, or code; (e) use the Service to send unsolicited commercial messages in violation of CAN-SPAM, TCPA, or similar law; (f) impersonate any person or business; (g) upload Client data you lack authority to upload; or (h) interfere with other Subscribers' use of the Service.

3.4 Conduct toward other Subscribers. The Service depends on businesses being able to trust the reporting and safety tools and to compete fairly. You may not:

  • File false or bad-faith reports. You may not submit a report about another Subscriber, practitioner, or Client that you know or should know is false, that is made for the purpose of harassing, retaliating against, or disrupting the business of another Subscriber, or that repeats a report already reviewed and closed without new information. Reports made in good faith that turn out to be mistaken are not a violation.
  • Impersonate or pass off as another business. You may not create or operate an account, profile, booking page, or service listing that uses another business's or practitioner's name, trade name, logo, photographs, practitioner names, reviews, or confusingly similar branding, or that states or implies an affiliation, succession ("formerly X"), or endorsement that does not exist, with the purpose or effect of diverting that business's Clients to you. Ordinary competition, including offering similar services at similar prices in the same area, is not a violation.
  • Interfere with another business's operations. You may not use the Service, directly or through others, to flood another Subscriber's booking page with bookings you do not intend to keep, to make repeated no-show or cancellation bookings, to submit abusive intake forms or messages, or to otherwise disrupt its schedule or staff.

If we determine after review under Section 4 that you have violated this Section, we may suspend or terminate your account, and the confidentiality in Section 4.2(d) will not protect you: we may disclose your identity and the substance of your reports or conduct to the Subscriber you targeted, so that it may pursue its own remedies, and you agree you are liable to KinesioCal for the costs of reviewing your reports and to the targeted Subscriber for the harm you caused.

If you believe you are being targeted. If you believe another Subscriber is impersonating your business, filing false reports against you, or interfering with your operations, contact us at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com with the account or listing involved and whatever evidence you have (screenshots, booking records, emails or texts you received). We will review under Section 4, keep your report confidential under Section 4.2(d), and tell you the outcome to the extent Section 4.2(d) allows. Where we confirm a violation of this Section, we will tell you so and may identify the responsible Subscriber to you as described above. Reporting under this paragraph is itself subject to the good-faith requirement in this Section.

4. Investigation, Enforcement, and Mandatory Reporting

4.1 Investigation. If we receive a report or detect indicators under Section 3.2, or have reason to believe an account was created by or for someone other than the person or business it claims to represent, we may review account content, booking records, practitioner profiles, and public licensing data, and may suspend the account, or specific features, while we review.

As part of a review we may require you, and any User on your account, to provide additional supporting documentation within a stated period, sent by email to KinesioCalendar@gmail.com (the Service has no upload for it), including: a government-issued photo ID (such as a state driver's license or identification card) for the account owner and for any practitioner whose identity or licensure is in question; business licenses, establishment permits, and registrations; professional licenses or credentials for each practitioner; and proof of authority to act for the business. Documentation you provide is used only to conduct the review, to make a report under Section 4.4, or to comply with legal process, and is handled as described in the Privacy Policy. Failure to provide requested documentation within the stated period is itself grounds for suspension or termination. Providing a document that is forged, altered, expired, issued to a different person, or that cannot be verified against the issuing authority's records is a violation of these Terms, and we may include such documents, together with the records that prompted the review, in any report made under Section 4.4 or in response to legal process.

Reviews without notice. Where we have a reasonable, good-faith belief that an account may involve human trafficking, sexual services, or services involving a minor, we may review the account and make a report under Section 4.4 without contacting you, without requesting documentation, and without suspending the account, because notice could endanger the people involved or interfere with a law-enforcement response. KinesioCal is not an investigative or law-enforcement body; in these cases our role is to pass what we have observed to the authorities whose role it is, and we may defer any further action on the account to their guidance. Nothing in Section 4.2 requires us to give notice or a response period before making such a report.

We will acknowledge your response and complete reviews as promptly as reasonably possible. Review time depends on the volume of reviews pending and on any response we are awaiting from a licensing board, law enforcement agency, or other third party, and we do not commit to a fixed timeline.

4.2 Fairness safeguards. Because false reports harm legitimate practices, we commit that: (a) no account will be terminated under Section 3.1 on an anonymous report alone without corroborating indicators (b) you will be told the general nature of the allegation and given 5 business days to respond before termination, unless we reasonably believe a person is in immediate danger or that notice would compromise an active law-enforcement matter; (c) a Subscriber suspended or terminated in error will be reinstated and will receive a prorated billing credit for the suspension period, or another billing adjustment; we do not issue refunds; and (d) reports are handled confidentially in both directions: we will not disclose the identity of a reporting party to you, and we will not disclose to a reporting party the outcome of a review or any action taken on your account beyond confirming that the report was received and reviewed, except where disclosure is required by law or legal process, or where we determine the report was made in bad faith under Section 3.4, in which case we may identify the reporting party to you.

4.3 Termination. Violation of Section 3.1 results in immediate, permanent termination of the account and all associated Users, forfeiture of prepaid fees, and we may refuse future accounts from the business, its owners, and its principals. Other violations may result in warning, suspension, or termination at our discretion.

4.4 Mandatory reporting. Reporting operates on two tracks.

  • Immediate reporting (no notice). If, after review, we have a reasonable, good-faith belief that an account is being used for sexual services, human trafficking, or services involving minors, we will report the account and relevant records to the appropriate state licensing board, local law enforcement, and, where trafficking is suspected, the National Human Trafficking Hotline or federal authorities. We may do so without notice to you.
  • Reporting after response window. If a practitioner on your account cannot be matched to a valid license and you fail to produce verifiable licensure within the response window in Section 4.2(b), we will report the practitioner and business to the licensing board of each state where services were offered.

You agree that reporting under this Section is not a breach of these Terms or the Privacy Policy.

4.5 Damages for illicit use. You acknowledge that use of the Service for the purposes prohibited by Section 3.1 causes KinesioCal harm that is real but difficult to quantify at the time of signing: investigation and legal costs; the cost of cooperating with authorities; potential liability to third parties; and reputational harm to the platform and its legitimate Subscribers, the repair of which requires public-relations, marketing, and customer-retention expenditure. You therefore agree that, in addition to termination and any other remedy, you will pay KinesioCal the greater of (a) liquidated damages of \$10,000 per violating account, which the parties agree is a reasonable pre-estimate of minimum harm and not a penalty, or (b) KinesioCal's actual damages, including documented reputational-remediation costs. In either case you will also pay KinesioCal's reasonable attorneys' fees and costs of investigation, enforcement, and collection.

4.6 Data retention after termination for cause. Notwithstanding Section 7, we may preserve records of an account terminated under Section 3.1 for as long as reasonably necessary to support investigations, legal proceedings, or reporting obligations.

5. Government, Law Enforcement, and Licensing Board Requests

This section states how KinesioCal handles requests for Subscriber Data from government agencies, law enforcement, and professional licensing boards ("Requesting Agencies"). It is also published separately as our Law Enforcement Request Policy.

5.1 Formal process required for non-public data. Except as provided in 5.3, we disclose non-public Subscriber Data to a Requesting Agency only in response to valid legal process: a subpoena, court order, search warrant, or a licensing board's statutory demand, served on KinesioCal, LLC by email to KinesioCalendar@gmail.com. Informal requests, phone calls, or requests addressed to a Subscriber's staff are not sufficient. We review every request for facial validity and scope, and we may narrow or challenge requests we consider overbroad.

5.2 Preservation. On a written preservation request from a Requesting Agency that identifies the account, the records, and a case or matter reference, we will preserve the identified records for 90 days pending legal process, without disclosing them. We will extend preservation for further 90-day periods on a written renewal that references the same matter, up to a total of one year from the original request. Beyond that, continued preservation requires legal process or a court order. Preservation means we hold the records and exempt them from deletion; held records may still be archived but remain retrievable. It does not give the Requesting Agency access to them, and copies are provided only under Section 5.1. Preserved records are released back to the normal retention schedule when the preservation period lapses without legal process, when the Requesting Agency withdraws the request, or when the matter closes. Because records are archived and deleted on an automated schedule in Section 7.4, a preservation request must reach us at least 30 days before a record's scheduled deletion date for us to guarantee preservation. We will make reasonable efforts to act on requests received inside that window, but we cannot guarantee that records already queued for deletion can be recovered, and we are not liable for records deleted on schedule before a request was received or could reasonably be acted on.

5.3 Voluntary and emergency disclosure. We may disclose Subscriber Data without legal process when we have a good-faith belief that disclosure is necessary to prevent imminent death or serious physical injury, or when we are making a report under Section 4.4.

5.4 Notice to Subscriber. We will notify the Subscriber of a request for its data before disclosure, unless (a) a court order or statute prohibits notice, (b) the request relates to a Section 4.4 report, or (c) we reasonably believe notice would endanger a person or obstruct an investigation. Where notice is delayed, we will provide it when the restriction lifts.

5.5 Decoy accounts, impersonation, and platform integrity. No person or entity, including any Requesting Agency, may create or operate a Subscriber account or a Client account for the purpose of impersonating a business or client, inducing or soliciting conduct prohibited by Section 3, or surveilling or investigating other users of the Service. Any such account is created in breach of these Terms, is void, and will be terminated on discovery regardless of who operates it. KinesioCal does not consent to and will not knowingly host a decoy account, and a Requesting Agency wishing to conduct any activity on the Service beyond ordinary public use of a booking portal must obtain KinesioCal's written agreement in advance. KinesioCal will consider written requests from Requesting Agencies for cooperation in good faith, and may enter into a written cooperation agreement on terms it determines. KinesioCal will not create, alter, or backdate Subscriber Data at any party's request and will not provide any party with a Subscriber's credentials, administrative interface, or non-public records except through the process in 5.1.

5.6 Protection of legitimate Subscribers. We recognize that licensed massage therapists are disproportionately targeted by false reports and inspection-based harassment. We will not act against a Subscriber solely because an inquiry was made, and we will not treat the existence of an inquiry as an indicator under Section 3.2. We keep a record of the requests we receive about each account. You may ask for it through the Contact support form in the app or at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com, and we will provide it where legally permitted, together with an attestation of your licensure data as entered by you in the Service, for use in responding to an inspection or complaint.

5.7 Transparency. We may, at our discretion, publish a periodic summary of the number and type of Requesting Agency requests received. Any such summary will be aggregated and will not identify any Subscriber, Client, or matter, and we may withhold or round figures small enough that an individual request could be inferred. Nothing in this Section obligates us to publish a summary for any period.

6. Subscriptions, Billing, and Payments

6.1 Plans and fees. The Service is sold as a monthly subscription with a flat base fee plus per-chair (per-practitioner seat) add-ons, in the tiers published on our Pricing page. Fees are billed in advance each month. Your subscription renews automatically each month until you cancel it. The Automatic Renewal Terms, a separate document shown in the app, state the price, the renewal, and how to cancel; you accept them each time you start or change a plan, and we keep a record of each acceptance. Upgrades, and adding seats, take effect immediately and are prorated. Downgrades to a lower plan, and reductions in seats, take effect at the end of the current billing period and are not prorated or credited: you keep the current plan and seats until then, and the new price starts on your next renewal. The listed price is the full amount charged; a plan listed at $60 bills $60. Any applicable taxes are included in that price. We may itemize or collect taxes separately in the future, or in particular states where required, on notice under Section 6.2.

6.2 Changes to pricing. We may change fees on 30 days' notice; changes apply at your next billing cycle after the notice period.

6.3 Cancellation and refunds. You may cancel at any time from account settings; cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period. Fees are non-refundable. Where we grant relief we do so as a prorated billing credit or other billing adjustment, decided case by case, or as required by law.

6.4 Late payment and unpaid accounts. If a payment fails, our payment processor retries the charge and we notify you by email and in the app. You then have a grace period of 3 days during which your portal access continues and you may export your records. After the grace period, every sign-in goes to your Account page, where you may reactivate your subscription at any time; the help pages and Contact support stay reachable, and your public booking page closes, telling Clients that the booking page is not available right now and to contact the business directly. Reactivating restores full access to your account, your booking page, and your data as it then stands; nothing is deleted by the lock itself. While the account is unpaid, you cannot export data from the portal and must request it from support. We reserve the right to delete the data of an unpaid account after the grace period, on the schedule in Section 7.4.

The grace period is a courtesy, not free service. Your billing date does not move: a payment made during or after the grace period covers the subscription period that began on your original billing date, including the grace days, and your next billing date is unchanged. If your subscription becomes past due more than three times in any rolling twelve-month period, we may terminate your account under Section 13 rather than offer a further grace period.

6.5 Chargebacks and payment disputes. If you believe a charge is wrong, contact us at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com first; we will review and may credit or adjust your billing where appropriate, decided case by case. We do not issue refunds. If you instead dispute an authorized subscription charge through your bank, card issuer, or payment processor (a "chargeback"), we will immediately lock your account and place it under review. No grace period applies. While the account is locked, you may not access the portal or use self-service export, and we hold your data under Section 7.4 pending the outcome. We do not withhold Client health records from the people who need them: during a lock we will still provide a Client's own records on request from that Client or from you for that Client's care, respond to legal process and licensing-board demands, and, once the dispute is resolved or the 90-day window in Section 7.4 applies, provide your full export through support without conditioning it on payment of the disputed amount. Reactivation of the account, as distinct from export, remains conditioned on payment. If the chargeback is withdrawn or decided in our favor, we will restore access on payment of any outstanding fees and the dispute fee charged to us. If the chargeback stands, the reversed amount is treated as non-payment for a period in which you used the Service, your account is terminated, and you remain liable for the fees, dispute fees, and collection costs as described in Section 14.4(c). We may decline to accept a new account from a business or owner with an unresolved chargeback.

6.6 Client payments; you are the merchant of record. The Service integrates with Stripe (or another processor you connect) so that Clients can pay you. KinesioCal takes no percentage of Client transactions and is not a party to any transaction between you and a Client. You are the merchant of record, you are solely responsible for your refund, no-show, and cancellation policies, chargebacks, the gift cards, packages, and memberships you sell (including the gift-card expiration and fee rules of the states where your Clients live), sales tax on your services, and compliance with the processor's terms, and you will indemnify KinesioCal for claims arising from those transactions.

6.7 Beta features. Features labeled beta, preview, or early access are provided as-is and may change or be withdrawn without notice.

7. Subscriber Data, Client Data, and HIPAA

7.1 Ownership. You own Subscriber Data. You grant KinesioCal a limited license to host, process, display, back up, and transmit Subscriber Data solely to provide the Service, support you, and comply with law. We claim no other rights in it.

7.2 Your responsibilities for Client data. You are the data controller for your records of your Clients. Your record of a Client is part of your business records, and you hold it under your own retention duties. A Client who claims portal access gets their own KinesioCal account holding their login and their own copy of their contact details, which they control, edit, and download; KinesioCal is the controller of that account, deals with that Client directly for notices and privacy requests about it, and your responsibilities under this Section do not extend to it. Through the portal a Client may send you updates to their contact details and may export the record you hold about them, but cannot alter or erase your records; a Client's request to change or delete your record of them comes to you, and you answer it under your own obligations. KinesioCal does not alter a Subscriber's records at a Client's request. You are solely responsible for knowing and complying with the privacy, consumer-protection, health-records, and biometric-privacy laws of every jurisdiction in which you operate or in which your Clients reside, including obtaining any consents those laws require, giving Clients your own privacy notice, responding to Client access or deletion requests, and ensuring the accuracy of what you enter. KinesioCal's features, defaults, and form templates are not legal advice and do not establish what the law requires of you.

Custom questions. You may add your own questions to your booking form (intake fields). These are questions on your booking form, not a separate form and not a health-history intake. Every question you add must be reasonably related to the services you provide. You will not use custom questions or any other feature to collect: (a) Social Security numbers, driver's license, passport, or other government identification numbers; (b) financial account or payment card numbers; (c) biometric identifiers or information of any kind, including fingerprints, face geometry, voiceprints, or scans of a Client's photo or identification document; or (d) information about race, religion, sexual orientation, immigration status, or similar protected characteristics, unless you have a lawful basis to collect it and bear full responsibility for doing so. KinesioCal may remove any question that violates this Section without notice. You are responsible for any claim, fine, or statutory damages arising from information you choose to collect, and the indemnity in Section 12 applies.

Client identity checks. You may require Clients to present a government-issued ID matching the booking name at the appointment, for the sole purpose of practitioner safety and preventing fraudulent bookings. If you enable this setting, the Service tells the Client at booking that ID will be checked on arrival. The check happens in person: nothing is uploaded to or stored in the Service except whether the ID was verified, who verified it, and when. You are the party requesting and reviewing the ID and are responsible for your own notice to Clients and for complying with any law governing identification requests in your jurisdiction. You will not record, photograph, or transcribe a Client's ID number into the Service, including in custom questions or notes; item (c) above continues to apply. The Service does not accept Client ID uploads and does not verify identity; if you want authenticated identity verification, you must obtain it from a third-party service outside the Service and are solely responsible for that service and its data.

7.3 HIPAA. KinesioCal is not currently HIPAA-certified or HIPAA-compliant. We are building the Service with the intent of becoming HIPAA-compliant in the future: it is designed with the HIPAA Security Rule as a reference standard (encrypted fields, an audit trail, idle sign-out, and least-access roles), but that work is not finished, takes time, and no government body certifies HIPAA compliance. KinesioCal does not represent that the Service currently meets every requirement of the Security Rule, makes no claim that using the Service makes your business HIPAA-compliant, and does not offer HIPAA compliance or a Business Associate Agreement at this time, on any plan. We do treat Client data as health information and protect it accordingly, and we never sell Client data or personal identifying information (see the Privacy Policy). The Privacy Policy lists the safeguards in place today and those still planned, and we will update it as safeguards are added. Whether you are a HIPAA covered entity depends on your own activities, principally whether you bill insurance electronically. If you are a covered entity, you must not store protected health information in the Service unless and until KinesioCal offers and signs a Business Associate Agreement with you. We will update these Terms if that changes.

7.4 Export, archiving, and deletion. You may export Subscriber Data at any time while your account is active, in standard formats. What your business needs to work today is never archived: Client profiles, notes, and consents of an active account, and your services, retail, rooms, staff, and settings. What is archived is past activity that is not needed to function today: logs, past appointments and transactions, and used-up commerce. Those records are archived 18 to 24 months after their date, depending on record type, and can be retrieved on request to support; any record may be permanently deleted 30 months after its date regardless of when it was last viewed or retrieved, and viewing or requesting a copy does not extend that period. If your account is closed for any reason, or becomes unpaid under Section 6.4, your portal access ends or is limited to reactivation; you may obtain a complete export of your Subscriber Data by contacting support within 90 days of closure or of the end of the grace period, after which we may delete the data from production systems, and backups age out on their normal cycle. Reactivating an unpaid account before deletion restores access to whatever data then remains. We may retain data longer under Section 4.6, legal holds, or for tax and Safety Network records. You remain responsible for meeting your own licensing-board record-retention requirements by exporting and keeping your records.

7.5 Backups. We maintain backups for disaster recovery. Backups are not a substitute for your own records retention obligations under licensing rules; you remain responsible for keeping records as your licensing board requires.

7.6 Aggregate data. We may use de-identified, aggregated data (for example, average booking lead time across all Subscribers) to operate and improve the Service. Aggregate data will never identify you or any Client.

7.7 Privacy Policy. Our Privacy Policy, incorporated by reference, explains how we handle personal information.

We may use automated and AI-assisted tools to triage and respond to requests. 14.1 Governing law. These Terms are governed by the laws of the State of Indiana, without regard to conflict-of-law rules, and by the Federal Arbitration Act as to Section 14.3.

14.2 Informal resolution first. Before starting any arbitration or lawsuit, the party with a claim will send the other a written notice describing the claim and the relief sought (to KinesioCal at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com; to you at your account email). The parties will attempt in good faith to resolve the dispute for 30 days after the notice. No proceeding may be started before that period ends, except a request for injunctive or other equitable relief under Section 14.4(b), which may be brought immediately.

14.3 Binding individual arbitration. Except as provided in 14.4, any dispute arising out of or relating to these Terms or the Service will be resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, before a single arbitrator, in Lake County, Indiana, or by video conference if the parties agree. The arbitrator's award is final and may be entered in any court with jurisdiction. Each party bears its own arbitration fees and costs except as the Rules or Section 14.6 provide.

14.4 Exceptions. The following may be brought in court without arbitration and, where stated, without waiting for the negotiation period in Section 14.2:

  • (b) Injunctive relief. Either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in court to protect intellectual property, Confidential Information, or the security of the Service, without first arbitrating and without waiting for the negotiation period.

KinesioCal may bring an action in court to collect subscription fees that are unpaid, or that were paid and later reversed through a chargeback, bank dispute, or payment-processor claim after you had used the Service for the period in question. A reversed payment for a period in which you used the Service is treated as non-payment for that period, and you are liable for the fees, any dispute or chargeback fees charged to KinesioCal, and collection costs. Filing a chargeback for a charge you authorized, instead of contacting us for a billing review, is a breach of these Terms.
  • (d) Prohibited use. Claims by KinesioCal arising from a violation of Section 3.1 (illicit services, trafficking, minors, unlicensed practice), Section 3.4 (impersonation and bad-faith reports), or the decoy-account prohibition in Section 5.5 may be brought in court, because such claims may involve criminal conduct, third parties, or the need for a public judgment. These claims are not subject to the negotiation period.
  • (e) Third-party claims. If a third party (including a Client, another Subscriber, or a government agency) brings a claim against KinesioCal in court arising from your use of the Service, KinesioCal may bring you into that proceeding or bring a related indemnity claim against you in that court, rather than arbitrating separately.

For any matter not subject to arbitration, the state and federal courts located in Lake County, Indiana, have exclusive jurisdiction, and you consent to venue there.

If the class waiver is found unenforceable as to a particular claim, that claim will proceed in court under 14.4, not in arbitration, and the remainder of this Section remains in effect.

14.6 Attorneys' fees. In any arbitration or proceeding under this Section, the prevailing party is entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees and costs from the other party, in addition to any other relief.

14.7 Time limit. Any claim arising out of these Terms or the Service must be brought within one year after the claim accrues, or it is permanently barred, to the extent permitted by law.
